'''Jerzy Kazimierz Baksalary''' (25 June 1944 – 8 March 2005) was a Polish [[mathematician]] who specialized in [[mathematical statistics]] and [[linear algebra]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Baksalary|first1=Oskar Maria|last2=Styan|first2=George P. H.|date=2005-11-15|title=Some comments on the life and publications of Jerzy K. Baksalary (1944–2005)|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|series=Tenth Special Issue (Part 2) on Linear Algebra and Statistics|language=en|volume=410|pages=3–53|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2005.08.011|issn=0024-3795|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 1990 he was appointed professor of mathematical sciences. He authored over 170 academic papers published and won one of the Ministry of National Education awards.<ref name="autonazwa1">{{Cite web |title=Biografia w "Głosie Uczelnianym Uniwersytetu Zielonogórskiego" |url=http://www.uz.zgora.pl/wydawnictwo/miesiecznik04-2005/04.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911155458/http://www.uz.zgora.pl/wydawnictwo/miesiecznik04-2005/04.pdf |archive-date=2012-09-11 |access-date=2018-11-21 |website=www.uz.zgora.pl |language=pl}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education (1944 – 1988) ===
Baksalary was born in [[Poznań, Poland]] on 25 June 1944.<ref name=":4" /> From 1969 to 1988, he worked at the [[Agricultural University of Poznań]].<ref name=":4" />

In 1975, Baksalary received a PhD degree from [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań]]; his thesis on [[linear statistical models]] was supervised by [[Tadeusz Caliński]].<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=Oskar Maria |last2=Styan |first2=George P.H. |date=2005 |title=Jerzy K. Baksalary (1944–2005) and his contributions to Image |url=https://homepages.tuni.fi/simo.puntanen/BakSty-Image-2005.pdf |journal=Image |language=en |volume=34 |pages=14–15}}</ref> He received a [[Habilitation]] in 1984, also from Adam Mickiewicz University, where his ''Habilitationsschrift'' was also on linear statistical models.<ref name=":4" />

=== Career (1988 – 2005) ===
In 1988, Baksalary joined the [[Tadeusz Kotarbiński Pedagogical University]] in [[Zielona Góra]], Poland, being the university's rector from 1990 to 1996.<ref name=":4" /> In 1990, he became a "Professor of Mathematical Sciences", a title received from the [[President of Poland]].<ref name=":4" /> For the 1989–1990 academic year, he moved to the [[University of Tampere]] in Finland.<ref name=":4" /> Later on, he joined the [[University of Zielona Góra]].<ref name=":4" />

=== 2005 death and legacy ===
Baksalary died in Poznań on 8 March 2005.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> His funeral was held there on 15 March 2005.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> There, Caliński praised Baksalary for his "contributions to the Poznań school of mathematical statistics and [[biometry]]".<ref name=":4" />

Memorial events in honor of Baksalary were also held at two conferences after his death:<ref name=":4" />

* The 14th International Workshop on Matrices and Statistics, held at [[Massey University]] in New Zealand from 29 March to 1 April 2005.
* The Southern Ontario Matrices and Statistics Days, held at the [[University of Windsor]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2005 |title=Southern Ontario Matrices and Statistics Days Program |url=https://homepages.tuni.fi/simo.puntanen/WindsorProgram-25may05.pdf |website=homepages.tuni.fi}}</ref> in Canada from 9 to 10 June 2005.

== Research ==
In 1979, Baksalary and [[Radosław Kala]] proved that the [[matrix equation]] <math>AX - YB = C</math> has a solution for some matrices ''X'' and ''Y'' if and only if <math>(I - A^-A)C(I - B^-B) = 0</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=J.K. |last2=Kala |first2=R. |date=June 1979 |title=The matrix equation AX − YB = C |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0024379579900041 |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |language=en |volume=25 |pages=41–43 |doi=10.1016/0024-3795(79)90004-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> (Here, <math>A^-</math> denotes some [[g-inverse]] of the matrix ''A''.) This is equivalent to a 1952 result by [[W. E. Roth]] on the same equation, which states that the equation has a solution iff the ranks of the [[block matrices]] <math>\begin{bmatrix}
  A & C\\
  0 & B\\
\end{bmatrix}</math> and <math>\begin{bmatrix}
 A & 0\\
 0 & B\\
\end{bmatrix}</math> are equal.<ref name=":0" />

In 1980, he and Kala extended this result to the matrix equation <math>AXB + CYD = E</math>, proving that it can be solved if and only if <math>K_GK_AE = 0, K_AER_D = 0, K_CER_B = 0, ER_BR_H = 0</math>, where <math>G := K_AC</math> and <math>H := DR_B</math>.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=J.K. |last2=Kala |first2=R. |date=April 1980 |title=The matrix equation AXB+CYD=E |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0024379580901895 |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |language=en |volume=30 |pages=141–147 |doi=10.1016/0024-3795(80)90189-5|url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{Rp|page=146}} (Here, the notation <math>K_M := I - MM^-</math>, <math>R_M := I - M^-M</math> is adopted for any matrix ''M''.<ref name=":1" />{{Rp|page=146}})

In 1981, Baksalary and Kala proved that for a [[Gauss-Markov model]] <math>\{y, X\beta, V\}</math>, where the vector-valued variable has expectation <math>X\beta</math> and variance ''V'' (a [[dispersion matrix]]), then for any function ''F'', a [[best linear unbiased estimator]] of <math>X\beta</math> which is a function of <math>Fy</math> exists iff <math>C(X)\subset C(TF')</math>. The condition is equivalent to stating that <math>r(X\vdots TF') = r(X)</math>, where <math>r(\cdot)</math> denotes the [[Rank (linear algebra)|rank]] of the respective matrix.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=J. K. |last2=Kala |first2=R. |date=July 1981 |title=Linear Transformations Preserving Best Linear Unbiased Estimators in a General Gauss-Markoff Model |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-9/issue-4/Linear-Transformations-Preserving-Best-Linear-Unbiased-Estimators-in-a-General/10.1214/aos/1176345533.full |journal=The Annals of Statistics |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=913–916 |doi=10.1214/aos/1176345533 |issn=0090-5364}}</ref>

In 1995, Baksalary and [[Sujit Kumar Mitra]] introduced the "left-star" and "right-star" [[partial orderings]] on the set of [[complex matrices]], which are defined as follows. The matrix ''A'' is below the matrix ''B'' in the left-star ordering, written <math>A ~*< B</math>, iff <math>A^*A = A^*B</math> and <math>\mathcal{M}(A)\subseteq \mathcal{M}(B)</math>, where <math>\mathcal{M}(\cdot)</math> denotes the [[column span]] and <math>A^*</math> denotes the [[conjugate transpose]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=Jerzy K. |last2=Mitra |first2=Sujit Kumar |date=1991-04-15 |title=Left-star and right-star partial orderings |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0024-3795%2891%2990326-R |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |volume=149 |pages=73–89 |doi=10.1016/0024-3795(91)90326-R |issn=0024-3795|url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{Rp|page=76}} Similarly, ''A'' is below ''B'' in the right-star ordering, written <math>A <*~ B</math>, iff <math>AA^* = BA^*</math> and <math>\mathcal{M}(A^*) \subseteq \mathcal{M}(B^*)</math>.<ref name=":2" />{{Rp|page=76}}

In 2000, Jerzy Baksalary and [[Oskar Maria Baksalary]] characterized all situations when a [[linear combination]] <math>P = c_1P_1 + c_2P_2</math> of two [[idempotent matrices]] can itself be idempotent.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Baksalary |first1=Jerzy K. |last2=Baksalary |first2=Oskar Maria |date=December 2000 |title=Idempotency of linear combinations of two idempotent matrices |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/S0024-3795(00)00225-1 |journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications |volume=321 |issue=1–3 |pages=3–7 |doi=10.1016/s0024-3795(00)00225-1 |issn=0024-3795|url-access=subscription }}</ref> These include three previously known cases <math>P = P_1 + P_2</math>, <math>P = P_1 - P_2</math>, or <math>P = P_2 - P_1</math>, previously found by Rao and Mitra (1971); and one additional case where <math>c_2 = 1 - c_1</math> and <math>(P_1 - P_2)^2 = 0</math>.<ref name=":3" />
